title: "Best By" Is Not an Expiration Date
editorialNotes: The 80% (NRDC 2013) and 20% / $580 figures are survey and estimate based (the brief says "an estimated"); $580 is 20% of the EPA $2,913. Rendered with citations; the 20% is hero type per the brief and may need to be demoted to qualitative by Adi.
Brief draws the sticker border in Signal Red; thread palette here is Ink Gray and Steel Blue so red only appears on the declared loss slide.

thread.element: BEST BY sticker peeling back until only a ghost outline remains

copy.headline: 80% of Americans have thrown away food based on a date the government didn't set.
copy.citation: NRDC "The Dating Game" report, 2013 (updated figures cited in 2022 ReFED Insights Engine).

copy.headline: There are three different date labels. They mean three different things. None of them mean "unsafe after this date."
items: Best By - quality estimate. Made by the manufacturer.
Sell By - stock rotation instruction. For the store, not you.
Use By - the closest to a real deadline. Still usually conservative.

copy.headline: The US has no federal law requiring date labels on most foods.
items: The FDA encouraged "Best If Used By" as a standard in 2017.
copy.body: When you throw food away early, you buy more sooner.

copy.heroNumberCaption: Date label confusion causes an estimated 20% of all household food waste in the US.
copy.body: On a $2,913 annual waste figure, that's $580/year thrown away because of a label that has no legal definition.
copy.citation: ReFED Insights Engine (2022); NRDC "The Dating Game" (2013, figures replicated in subsequent studies).

copy.headline: The actual test for whether food is safe has nothing to do with a label.
items: Smell it. Off means off - your nose is reliable.
Look at it. Mold, slime, or discoloration = toss.
Texture check. Mushy where it should be firm = gone.
copy.body: If it passes all three: it's fine.

copy.headline: The most over-tossed foods in American kitchens - and how long they actually last after the label date:
items: Bread - 5-7 days past "Best By" (or freeze it)
copy.citation: FDA Refrigerator & Freezer Storage Chart; USDA FoodKeeper App data; food science consensus for dry pasta, cheese, eggs.

copy.headline: The label tells you when the manufacturer stops being responsible for quality. It says nothing about when the food stops being safe.
copy.ctaLine: fond tracks real shelf life - not label dates. Link in bio.
